title: Numerically stable softmax and additive log-ratio derivatives
text: softmax score vector \(\boldsymbol{z}\\mathbb{R}^{K}\) evaluated log-sum-exp (LSE) avoid overflow, \[ s_i=\operatorname{softmax}(\boldsymbol{z})_i=\frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum_{k}e^{z_k}} =e^{z_i-\operatorname{LSE}(\boldsymbol{z})}, \qquad \operatorname{LSE}(\boldsymbol{z})=m+\log\!\sum_{k}e^{z_k-m}, \quad m=\max_k z_k. \tag{1}\] Listing 1: Stable log-sum-exp softmax R Listing 2: Softmax log-sum-exp PyTorch softmax Jacobian difference diagonal rank-one term, \[ \frac{\partial s_i}{\partial z_j}=s_i(\delta_{ij}-s_j), \qquad \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{softmax}}=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{s}) -\boldsymbol{s}\boldsymbol{s}^{\top}. \tag{2}\] matrix also equals Hessian log-sum-exp, \(\nabla^2\operatorname{LSE}(\boldsymbol{z})=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{s}) -\boldsymbol{s}\boldsymbol{s}^{\top}\). softmax vector-valued, second derivative third-order tensor \(H_{ijk}=\partial^2 s_i/(\partial z_j\partial z_k)\), \[ H_{ijk}=s_i\bigl[(\delta_{ij}-s_j)(\delta_{ik}-s_k)-s_j(\delta_{jk}-s_k)\bigr], \tag{3}\] , slice slice, rank-one correction \[ \mathbf{H}^{()}=s_i\Bigl[(\boldsymbol{e}_i-\boldsymbol{s}) (\boldsymbol{e}_i-\boldsymbol{s})^{\top} -\bigl(\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{s})-\boldsymbol{s}\boldsymbol{s}^{\top}\bigr) \Bigr], \tag{4}\] \(\boldsymbol{e}_i\) \(\)-th canonical basis vector. Listing 3 materialises Eq. 2 Eq. 4 \(O(K^2)\) per slice. Listing 3: Softmax Jacobian Hessian tensor R Listing 4: Batched softmax Jacobian Hessian PyTorch
code: log_sum_exp <- function(z) {   m <- max(z)   m + log(sum(exp(z - m))) }  softmax <- function(z) {   exp(z - log_sum_exp(z)) } import torch import torch.nn.functional as F   def softmax(z: torch.Tensor, dim: int = -1) -> torch.Tensor:     return F.softmax(z, dim=dim)   def log_sum_exp(z: torch.Tensor, dim: int = -1) -> torch.Tensor:     return torch.logsumexp(z, dim=dim) softmax_jacobian <- function(z) {   s <- softmax(z)   diag(s) - tcrossprod(s) }  softmax_hessian <- function(z) {   s <- softmax(z)   k <- length(s)   jac <- diag(s) - tcrossprod(s)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(k, k, k))   for (i in seq_len(k)) {     di <- (seq_len(k) == i) - s # e_i - s     hessian[i, , ] <- s[i] * (tcrossprod(di) - jac)   }   hessian } def softmax_jacobian(z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """z: [..., K] -> [..., K, K]."""     s = softmax(z, dim=-1)     return torch.diag_embed(s) - s.unsqueeze(-1) * s.unsqueeze(-2)   def softmax_hessian(z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """z: [K] -> H[i, j, k] of shape [K, K, K]."""     s = softmax(z, dim=0)     eye = torch.eye(s.numel(), dtype=s.dtype, device=s.device)     diff = eye - s  # (e_i - s) stacked over i     outer = diff.unsqueeze(-1) * diff.unsqueeze(-2)     jac = torch.diag(s) - torch.outer(s, s)     return s[:, None, None] * (outer - jac.unsqueeze(0))

title: Numerically stable softmax and additive log-ratio derivatives
text: Let \(\boldsymbol{p}=(p_1,\ldots,p_J)\) composition \(p_j>0\) \(\sum_j p_j=1\), take last part \(J\) reference. additive log-ratio (alr) transform sends composition \(\mathbb{R}^{J-1}\), \[ \rho_i=\log\!\Bigl(\frac{p_i}{p_J}\Bigr),\qquad =1,\ldots,J-1, \tag{5}\] inverse, additive logistic transform (\(\mathrm{alr}^{-1}\)), pins reference logit zero, \(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\rho}}=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_{J-1},0)\), applies softmax, \[ \boldsymbol{p}=\operatorname{softmax}(\tilde{\boldsymbol{\rho}}), \qquad p_i=\frac{e^{\rho_i}}{1+\sum_{j<J}e^{\rho_j}}\ (<J), \qquad p_J=\frac{1}{1+\sum_{j<J}e^{\rho_j}}. \tag{6}\] Listing 5: Additive logistic additive log-ratio maps R Listing 6: Additive logistic additive log-ratio maps PyTorch additive logistic map softmax restricted first \(J-1\) inputs, Jacobian \(\mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}\\mathcal{M}_{J\times(J-1)}\) softmax Jacobian reference column dropped, \[ \frac{\partial p_i}{\partial\rho_a}=p_i(\delta_{ia}-p_a), \qquad \mathbf{J}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}} =\bigl[\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{p}) -\boldsymbol{p}\boldsymbol{p}^{\top}\bigr]_{:,\,1:(J-1)}, \qquad =1,\ldots,J-1. \tag{7}\] Hessian tensor \(\mathbf{H}_{\boldsymbol{\psi}}\\mathcal{M}_{J\times(J-1)\times(J-1)}\), softmax Hessian Eq. 4 restricted first \(J-1\) input indices, \[ \frac{\partial^2 p_i}{\partial\rho_a\partial\rho_b} =p_i\bigl[(\delta_{ia}-p_a)(\delta_{ib}-p_b)-p_a(\delta_{ab}-p_b)\bigr], \qquad ,b=1,\ldots,J-1. \tag{8}\] Listing 7: Jacobian Hessian additive logistic map R Jacobian \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{alr}}\\mathcal{M}_{(J-1)\times J}\) sparse, \[ \frac{\partial\rho_i}{\partial p_j}=\frac{\delta_{ij}}{p_i}-\frac{\delta_{jJ}}{p_J}, \qquad \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{alr}} =\Bigl[\operatorname{diag}\!\bigl(p_1^{-1},\ldots,p_{J-1}^{-1}\bigr) \ \big|\ -p_J^{-1}\boldsymbol{1}_{J-1}\Bigr], \tag{9}\] Hessian \(\mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{alr}}\\mathcal{M}_{(J-1)\times J\times J}\) diagonal last two modes, \[ \frac{\partial^2\rho_i}{\partial p_j\partial p_k} =-\frac{\delta_{ij}\delta_{ik}}{p_i^{2}} +\frac{\delta_{jJ}\delta_{kJ}}{p_J^{2}}. \tag{10}\] Listing 9: Jacobian Hessian additive log-ratio map R Listing 10: Jacobian Hessian additive log-ratio map PyTorch
code: # rho -> p  (additive logistic, alr^{-1}); reference logit appended as 0 additive_logistic <- function(rho) {   softmax(c(rho, 0)) }  # p -> rho  (additive log-ratio, alr); last part as reference additive_log_ratio <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   log(p[-j] / p[j]) } def additive_logistic(rho: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """rho: [..., J-1] -> p: [..., J] (reference category = last)."""     reference = torch.zeros_like(rho[..., :1])     return torch.softmax(torch.cat([rho, reference], dim=-1), dim=-1)   def additive_log_ratio(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [..., J] -> rho: [..., J-1]."""     log_p = torch.log(p)     return log_p[..., :-1] - log_p[..., -1:] additive_logistic_jacobian <- function(rho) {   p <- additive_logistic(rho)   j <- length(p)   (diag(p) - tcrossprod(p))[, -j, drop = FALSE] }  additive_logistic_hessian <- function(rho) {   p <- additive_logistic(rho)   j <- length(p)   jac <- diag(p) - tcrossprod(p)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(j, j - 1, j - 1))   for (i in seq_len(j)) {     di <- (seq_len(j) == i) - p     slice <- p[i] * (tcrossprod(di) - jac)     hessian[i, , ] <- slice[-j, -j]   }   hessian } def additive_logistic_jacobian(rho: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """rho: [J-1] -> Jacobian [J, J-1]."""     p = additive_logistic(rho)     return (torch.diag(p) - torch.outer(p, p))[:, :-1]   def additive_logistic_hessian(rho: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """rho: [J-1] -> Hessian [J, J-1, J-1]."""     reference = torch.zeros_like(rho[:1])     augmented = torch.cat([rho, reference])     return softmax_hessian(augmented)[:, :-1, :-1] additive_log_ratio_jacobian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   idx <- seq_len(j - 1)   jac <- matrix(0, j - 1, j)   jac[cbind(idx, idx)] <- 1 / p[idx]   jac[, j] <- -1 / p[j]   jac }  additive_log_ratio_hessian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(j - 1, j, j))   for (i in seq_len(j - 1)) {     hessian[i, i, i] <- -1 / p[i]^2     hessian[i, j, j] <- 1 / p[j]^2   }   hessian } def additive_log_ratio_jacobian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Jacobian [J-1, J]."""     j = p.numel()     jac = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     jac[idx, idx] = 1.0 / p[:-1]     jac[:, -1] = -1.0 / p[-1]     return jac   def additive_log_ratio_hessian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Hessian [J-1, J, J]."""     j = p.numel()     hessian = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     hessian[idx, idx, idx] = -1.0 / p[:-1].square()     hessian[:, -1, -1] = 1.0 / p[-1].square()     return hessian

title: Additive logistic transform (unconstrained coordinates to the simplex) — additive_logistic
text: Implements reparametrisation \(\boldsymbol{\psi}:\boldsymbol{\rho}\mapsto\boldsymbol{p}\) used article, sending unconstrained coordinates \(\boldsymbol{\rho}\\mathbb{R}^{J-1}\) cellular proportions \(\boldsymbol{p}\\Delta^{J-1}\). additive logistic transform Aitchison, .e. inverse additive log-ratio map (\(\mathrm{alr}^{-1}\)), equivalently softmax last category \(J\) pinned reference (\(\rho_J\equiv 0\)). Recovers unconstrained additive log-ratio coordinates \(\rho_j=\ln(p_j/p_J)\) \(j=1,\ldots,J-1\), last part \(p_J\) reference. Aitchison's additive log-ratio (\(\mathrm{alr}\)) transform, equivalently multinomial-logit link reference category \(J\) (see compositions::alr()).

text: Estimates \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}=\arg\max_{\boldsymbol{p}} \ell_{\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,\boldsymbol{\zeta}}(\boldsymbol{p})\) Gaussian convolution model $$   \boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})   \sim\mathcal{N}_{G}\!\bigl(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p},\,   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\bigr),   \qquad   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j, $$ subject simplex constraint \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{p}=1\), \(\boldsymbol{p}\ge\mathbf{0}\). title: Simulate hierarchical GRN first- and second-order moments — simulate_hierarchical_grn_moments
text: Builds mean matrices \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) covariance arrays \((\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)\) parent/child cell populations graph-constrained precision model. Parent means use complementary block structure; child means \(\boldsymbol{\mu}^{(k)}=\boldsymbol{\mu}^{(\mathrm{parent})}+\boldsymbol{\delta}^{(k)}\) \(\boldsymbol{\delta}^{(k)}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\sigma_\delta^{2}\mathbf{})\). Marginal variances follow \(\sigma_g^{2}=\mu_g+\mu_g^{\alpha}/L\); covariances obtained shared normalised precision \(\boldsymbol{\Omega}\) via \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k=\mathbf{D}_k^{1/2}\mathbf{R}\mathbf{D}_k^{1/2}\) \(\mathbf{R}=\mathrm{cov2cor}(\boldsymbol{\Omega}^{-1})\).
